blocks.text: Structural isomerism is shown by all classes of organic compounds and their derivatives, not only hydrocarbons; it arises from the difference in the arrangement of atoms within the molecule and is exhibited in five ways.

items: Chain isomerism arises from a difference in the nature of the carbon chain: butane and 2-methylpropane (isobutane) for C4H10; pentane, 2-methylbutane (isopentane) and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane) for C5H12.
Position isomerism arises from a difference in the position of the same functional group on an unchanged carbon chain: 1-chloropropane and 2-chloropropane; but-1-ene and but-2-ene (C4H8).
Functional group isomerism: compounds with the same molecular formula but different functional groups, such as methoxymethane CH3OCH3 and ethanol CH3CH2OH (C2H6O).

Metamerism arises from the unequal distribution of carbon atoms on either side of the functional group in compounds of the same homologous series: ethoxyethane CH3CH2OCH2CH3 and methoxypropane CH3OCH2CH2CH3; for the ketone C5H10O, pentan-3-one CH3CH2COCH2CH3 and pentan-2-one CH3COCH2CH2CH3.

Tautomerism arises from the shifting of a proton from one atom to another in the same molecule, commonly seen in amino acids, which exist as zwitterions formed when a proton moves from the carboxylic acid end to the amine group: RCH(NH2)COOH and RCH(NH3+)COO-.

blocks.text: Stereoisomers have the same structural formula but differ in the positions of identical groups in space. There are two types, geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism and optical isomerism; they belong to the Class XII syllabus.

blocks.prompt: Name an isomer of C4H8 showing position isomerism, say what type of isomers ethoxymethane and propanol are, and list the structural isomerism possible in alkenes (Quick Check 11.9a to c).
blocks.explanation: But-1-ene CH2=CHCH2CH3 and but-2-ene CH3CH=CHCH3 are position isomers of C4H8. Ethoxymethane CH3CH2OCH3 and propan-1-ol CH3CH2CH2OH are both C3H8O with different functional groups (ether and alcohol): functional group isomers. Alkenes can show chain isomerism (but-1-ene and 2-methylpropene), position isomerism (but-1-ene and but-2-ene) and functional group isomerism with cycloalkanes (but-1-ene and cyclobutane).

items: Structural isomerism: chain (butane / isobutane), position (1- / 2-chloropropane, but-1-ene / but-2-ene), functional group (ethanol / methoxymethane), metamerism (ethoxyethane / methoxypropane, pentan-2-one / pentan-3-one), tautomerism (amino acid / zwitterion).
Stereoisomerism: same structure, different arrangement in space; geometrical (cis-trans) and optical, in Class XII.
